dhammavimalamādāsaṃ.meaning_2: pure mirror of the Dhamma; stainless mirror of the teaching
dhammavimalamādāsaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text. The compound sandhi is vimala + ādāsa > vimalamādāsa. Epithet for the Dhamma as a mirror reflecting the truth.
dhammavimalamādāsaṃ.translation_1: Having placed the pure Dhamma-mirror for the multitudes of beings,

nidassayi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 3rd singular nidassayi in the verse, from the causative stem nidassayati (ni + dis + *aya). The PEU entry nidassayi [ni+disa+ṇaya+ī] is a different analysis; the reading is aorist here.

laḷanto.meaning_2: playing; sporting; frolicking; enjoying oneself; shining
laḷanto.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Nominative singular in the text, describing the Buddha approaching by psychic power like a sporting deva. Some texts read lalanto.
laḷanto.translation_1: approached by psychic power, like a shining deva in the sky.

assattharukkhamūlamhi.meaning_2: root of the Assattha tree; foot of the Bodhi tree
assattharukkhamūlamhi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative singular in the text. Assattha is the Bodhi tree (Ficus religiosa) under which the Buddha awakened.
assattharukkhamūlamhi.translation_1: the Great Famed One (mahāyaso) will awaken (bujjhissati) at the root of the Assattha tree (Assattharukkhamūlamhi).

bhavantvantarāyā.meaning_2: may there be obstacles; let there be obstacles; may obstacles befall
bhavantvantarāyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of bhavantu (imperative 3rd plural of bhavati) + antarāyā (nominative plural of antarāya). In the text preceded by mā, so negated: 'may there be no obstacles'; some editions read bhavatvantarāyo (singular).
bhavantvantarāyā.example_1: Mā te bhavantvantarāyā [bhavatvantarāyo (sī. syā.)], phusa khippaṃ bodhimuttamaṃ.
bhavantvantarāyā.translation_1: May no obstacles befall you; quickly attain the supreme enlightenment.”

virajjhiya.meaning_2: having missed; having failed (to); having neglected; having avoided
virajjhiya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive in -iya (cf. -itvā) from vi + √rādh (succeed, accomplish), here in the negative sense 'missing, failing to reach' (paṭititthaṃ). The PEU suggests √radh/rādh + ya + tvā.
virajjhiya.example_1: 73. ‘‘ Yathā manussā nadiṃ tarantā, paṭititthaṃ virajjhiya;
virajjhiya.translation_1: ‘Just as (yathā) humans (manussā) crossing (tarantā) a river (nadiṃ), having missed (virajjhiya) the opposite ford (paṭititthaṃ);

jinapabhuttamaṃ.meaning_2: supreme radiance of the Conqueror; supreme splendour of the Buddha
jinapabhuttamaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound of jina (the Conqueror, i.e. the Buddha), pabhā (radiance) and uttama (supreme), with pabhā shortened to pabhu before uttama. Accusative singular in the text, dependent on patvā.
jinapabhuttamaṃ.example_1: Sabbāpi tā hatā honti, patvā jinapabhuttamaṃ.
jinapabhuttamaṃ.translation_1: all of them are overcome, having reached the supreme radiance of the Conqueror.

upanissā.meaning_2: having heard the one who teaches; having listened to the teacher
upanissā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading (syā., kaṃ.) of upanisādino in the Buddhavaṃsa verse; probably a sandhi/scribal form of upanisādin, 'one who sits near, a teacher', or a misreading, not a separate word.
upanissā.example_1: 6. Sabbākārena bhāsato, sutvā upanisādino [upanissā jino (syā. kaṃ.)];
upanissā.translation_1: 6. Having heard from the one who taught in every way,

arahasī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 2nd singular present of arahati (replaced by arahasī in verse). Takes the genitive/accusative of the thing deserved: sabbaṃ arahasī = you are worthy of all.
arahasī.translation_1: and bowing down and offerings — you are worthy of all these.

tipāṭihīre.meaning_2: three miracles; threefold miraculous power (psychic power, mind-reading, and instruction)
tipāṭihīre.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative singular in the text. Refers to the threefold miracle (iddhi, ādesanā, anusāsanī).
tipāṭihīre.example_2: 11. Iddhī ca ādesanānusāsanī, tipāṭihīre bhagavā vasī ahu;
tipāṭihīre.translation_2: 11. The Blessed One was master in the three miracles: psychic power, mind-reading, and instruction.

medisaṃ.meaning_2: such; of this kind; like this
medisaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular modifying a neuter noun in the text. Possibly a sandhi of ima + disa; the reading medisaṃ is unusual, and medinī (earth) does not fit the context.
medisaṃ.translation_2: I have never before seen such a wonderful and hair-raising thing!”

ḍeṇḍimā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant spelling of ḍiṇḍima; nominative plural in the verse. One of several drums listed with saṅkha and paṇava.
ḍeṇḍimā.example_1: 32. Saṅkhā ca paṇavā ceva, athopi ḍiṇḍimā [ḍeṇḍimā (sī.)] bahū;
ḍeṇḍimā.translation_1: 32. Conch shells and kettle drums, and also many other drums,

hiṅkārā.meaning_2: sound of "hiṅ"; exclamation of approval; shout of "hiṅ"
hiṅkārā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Nominative plural in the text, paired with sādhukārā. Probably an onomatopoeic noun; treated here as a compound of the exclamation hiṅ + kāra, so the root fields are doubtful.
hiṅkārā.example_2: 35. Hiṅkārā sādhukārā ca [hiṅkāraṃ sādhukārañca (sī. syā.)], ukkuṭṭhi sampahaṃsanaṃ [sampasādanaṃ (sī.), sampanādanaṃ (syā.)];
hiṅkārā.translation_2: 35. “Sounds of 'hing', shouts of 'sādhu', acclamations, and great delight

sampanādanaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading (syā.) for sampahaṃsanaṃ / sampasādanaṃ in the verse. Probably saṃ + panādana, from √pad (go) or √nand (delight). Nominative singular here.
sampanādanaṃ.example_1: 35. Hiṅkārā sādhukārā ca [hiṅkāraṃ sādhukārañca (sī. syā.)], ukkuṭṭhi sampahaṃsanaṃ [sampasādanaṃ (sī.), sampanādanaṃ (syā.)];
sampanādanaṃ.translation_1: 35. “Sounds of 'hing', shouts of 'sādhu', acclamations, and great delight

sannipātayi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 3rd singular in the text, with i ending (sannipātayi). Causative of sannipatati.
sannipātayi.translation_2: those with taints destroyed, stainless, he assembled in an instant.”

koraṇḍasamasādiso.meaning_2: whose appearance is like the koraṇḍa flower; resembling the koraṇḍa blossom
koraṇḍasamasādiso.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Epithet of Sāriputta in Buddhavaṃsa verse 57, describing his complexion. Nominative singular in -o; lemma_2 given as the stem form.
koraṇḍasamasādiso.translation_2: Sāriputta, who was wise, whose complexion was like a koraṇḍa flower,

karavīkamadhuragiro.meaning_2: whose voice is as sweet as a karavīka bird's; with a voice sweet as the karavīka bird
karavīkamadhuragiro.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Epithet of the Buddha in Buddhavaṃsa verse. Vocative singular in the text; the -o ending is the sandhi of -a with the following word. Bahubbīhi compound.
karavīkamadhuragiro.translation_2: Being asked by him, he answered with a voice as sweet as a karavīka bird,

bherisaṅkharathāni.meaning_2: drums, conches and chariots; the sound of drums, conches and chariots
bherisaṅkharathāni.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A dvanda compound in the plural, neuter nominative/accusative, listed among the sounds heard (hatthisaddaṃ assasaddaṃ ... ca). Sometimes analysed as three separate items rather than one compound.
bherisaṅkharathāni.translation_2: the sound of elephants, the sound of cavalry, and the sounds of drums, conches, and chariots,

yaṃnūnimaṃ.meaning_2: what if I (were to) ... this; surely, let me ... this (rotten body)
yaṃnūnimaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of yaṃ (that) + nūna (indeed, now) + imaṃ (this), an idiom expressing resolve or self-encouragement. Often written yaṃ nūn' imaṃ. First word of the verse; metrically yaṃnūni 'maṃ is also possible (nūni = nūna).
yaṃnūnimaṃ.translation_2: ‘Surely, if I were to abandon this rotten body, filled with various foul things,

pariruddho.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Past participle of parirundhati, used in the text with arīhi (instrumental plural, 'by enemies'). Looks nominative singular masculine in form.
pariruddho.translation_2: Just as when a path for travel exists for one surrounded by enemies;

kilesapariruddho.meaning_2: obstructed by defilements; blocked by mental impurities; surrounded by defilements
kilesapariruddho.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Bahubbīhi compound with kilesa. Nominative singular used in the verse; describes a person hemmed in by defilements.
kilesapariruddho.translation_2: So too, when a safe path exists for one surrounded by defilements;

udakagāhiṇiṃ.meaning_2: taking in water; leaking; letting water in
udakagāhiṇiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text, agreeing with nāvaṃ. Sinhalese edition reads udagāhiṇiṃ; the word is a compound with udaka (water) + gāhinī (taking).
udakagāhiṇiṃ.example_1: 23. ‘‘ Yathāpi jajjaraṃ nāvaṃ, paluggaṃ udagāhiniṃ [udakagāhiṇiṃ (sī.), udakagāhiniṃ (syā.)];
udakagāhiṇiṃ.translation_1: Just as a brittle (jajjaraṃ), crumbling (paluggaṃ), leaking (udakagāhiniṃ) boat;

apphoṭhenti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative in form with passive-like -ya in some instances, but here active 3rd singular. Variant reading apphoṭenti (plural) given in commentarial edition; the text's apphoṭhenti is likely a sandhi of apphoṭheti + ti or a scribal variant. The word describes clapping hands as a sign of joy.
apphoṭhenti.translation_1: Shouts of acclamation (ukkuṭṭhisaddā) arose (vattanti); they were clapping their hands (apphoṭenti) and (ca) smiling (hasanti);

paṭititthaṃ.meaning_2: opposite ford; ford on the other side; far bank
paṭititthaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text ('the opposite ford'). The word is a bahubbīhi-like compound carrying an adjective sense ('on the other side'), but the PEU guide treats it as nt.
paṭititthaṃ.example_2: 73. ‘‘ Yathā manussā nadiṃ tarantā, paṭititthaṃ virajjhiya;
paṭititthaṃ.translation_2: ‘Just as (yathā) humans (manussā) crossing (tarantā) a river (nadiṃ), having missed (virajjhiya) the opposite ford (paṭititthaṃ);

dakajā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Tatpurisa compound with ja from √jan. In the verse it describes flowers (pupphā); the form is nominative plural.
dakajā.example_2: 86. ‘‘‘ Thalajā dakajā pupphā, sabbe pupphanti tāvade;
dakajā.translation_2: ‘“All (sabbe) land-born (thalajā) and water-born (dakajā) flowers (pupphā) immediately (tāvade) bloomed (pupphanti);

tepajjubho.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of tepi (te + pi) and ubho; nominative plural, the subject of abhiravanti. Sometimes written te pajjubho in editions.
tepajjubho.translation_2: And today (ajja), both (ubho) of those (tepi) resound (abhiravanti). You will certainly (dhuvaṃ) be a Buddha (buddho bhavissasi).”’

tampajjubbhijjate.meaning_2: and that springs up today (from); and that today wells up (from)
tampajjubbhijjate.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of taṃ + api + ajja + ubbhijjate; the verb is passive/present of ubbhijjati (springs up). Locative mahiyā in the text.
tampajjubbhijjate.translation_2: And today (ajja), that (tampi) water springs up (ubbhijjate) from the earth (mahiyā). You will certainly (dhuvaṃ) be a Buddha (buddho bhavissasi).”’

sopajja.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of so + ajja. Used in the verse describing the fragrance that wafts today.
sopajja.example_2: Sopajja vāyati gandho, dhuvaṃ buddho bhavissasi.
sopajja.translation_2: And today (ajja), that (so) fragrance (gandho) wafts (vāyati). You will certainly (dhuvaṃ) be a Buddha (buddho bhavissasi).”’

vudakaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Probably a sandhi or variant form of udakaṃ; appears as 'vudakaṃ' in the verse. Accusative singular in the text.
vudakaṃ.example_1: Vamate vudakaṃ nissesaṃ, na tattha parirakkhati.
vudakaṃ.translation_1: it empties all the water (udakaṃ nissesaṃ) without residue (nissesaṃ), and does not retain (na parirakkhati) any (tattha) of it.

paṭilaggitaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Neuter nominative singular in the verse, agreeing with vālaṃ (tail). The same form used in the simile of the chamarī deer's tail. The PEU entry takes paṭilaggita as 'entangled, caught'; possibly the reading is paṭilagita. The prefix is paṭi, not pati.
paṭilaggitaṃ.translation_2: Just as (yathāpi) a chamari deer (camarī), if its tail (vālaṃ) is caught (paṭilaggitaṃ) on anything (kismiñci);

sañcuṇṇamathitā.meaning_2: shattered and crushed; crushed to pieces
sañcuṇṇamathitā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Descriptive compound modifying subjects in the verse; nominative plural in the text.
sañcuṇṇamathitā.translation_2: colliding with each other there, were shattered and crushed.

koṭisatamabodhayi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi with koṭisataṃ; aorist 3rd singular of the causative bodheti. In the text: 'koṭisataṃ abodhayi' = awakened a hundred koṭis.
koṭisatamabodhayi.translation_2: 8. At the first Dhamma-penetration, the Buddha awakened one hundred million beings;

upasoṇo.meaning_2: name of a chief lay follower of Buddha Koṇḍañña; Upasoṇa
upasoṇo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name; nominative singular in the text. One of the two aggupaṭṭhāka (chief attendants) of Buddha Koṇḍañña, together with Soṇa.
upasoṇo.example_2: 32. Soṇo ca upasoṇo ca, ahesuṃ aggupaṭṭhakā;
upasoṇo.translation_2: 32. Soṇa and Upasoṇa were the chief male lay followers;

sīvalo.meaning_2: name of a thera (son of Buddha Maṅgala); Sīvala
sīvalo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name. Nominative singular in the text in the phrase sīvalo nāma atrajo (son of Yasavatī).
sīvalo.example_2: Yasavatī nāma nārī, sīvalo nāma atrajo.
sīvalo.translation_2: The woman was called Yasavatī, and his son was called Sīvala.

anulā.meaning_2: Anulā; name of a female lay disciple; name of a nun
anulā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name, nominative singular in the text; sometimes spelled Anuḷā. The reading anulā is a sandhi of anulā + ca; the entry is for the name itself.
anulā.example_2: Anulā ceva sutanā ca, ahesuṃ aggupaṭṭhikā.
anulā.translation_2: Anulā and Sutanā were the chief female lay followers.

upasoṇā.meaning_2: name of a female disciple; Upasoṇā
upasoṇā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name. In the Buddhavaṃsa, Soṇā and Upasoṇā were the two chief female disciples of Buddha Koṇḍañña. Nominative singular in the text.
upasoṇā.example_2: 27. Soṇā ca upasoṇā ca, ahesuṃ aggasāvikā;
upasoṇā.translation_2: 27. Soṇā and Upasoṇā were his chief female disciples;

bodhayi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 3rd singular of the causative bodheti, used actively with an object (bodhanīye). PEU's analysis Budha+ṇaya+ī is not followed.
bodhayi.translation_2: 31. Having saved those who were to be saved, and enlightened those who were to be enlightened,

atthami.meaning_2: setting (of the sun or moon); having set; at the setting (of)
atthami.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of atthaṃ + i (or atthaṃ + iti), literally 'gone to setting'. Used of the moon setting: uḷurājāva atthami 'like the moon setting'. Sometimes written atthaṅgami; cf. atthaṅgama.
atthami.translation_2: the Perfectly Enlightened One attained final Nibbāna, like the moon setting.

thomayitvā.meaning_2: having praised; having lauded; having extolled
thomayitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive in -itvā from the causative thometi. Used in the verse with yathāthāmaṃ, 'according to my ability'. PEU splits it as thoma + ṇaya + tvā.
thomayitvā.translation_2: having praised them according to my ability, I offered my upper robe.

niyyādayī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 3rd singular of niyyādeti (< ni + yā + √dā, caus); often 'offered (to)'. The text has 'buddhe niyyādayī' = offered to the Buddha(s). The spelling -yādayī shows the causative stem with -y-.
niyyādayī.translation_2: having established a monastery, then offered it to the Buddha.

pugagaṇo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading pugagaṇo; the word is a compound of pura + gaṇa. Nominative singular here.
pugagaṇo.translation_1: 10. Furthermore, the townspeople gave a gift to the Buddha, supreme among men;

tamevatthamanuppattiyā.meaning_2: for the attainment of that very goal; for the accomplishment of just that matter
tamevatthamanuppattiyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of taṃ eva atthaṃ anuppattiyā (instrumental of anuppatti). In the verse it expresses the purpose: 'for the attainment of that very goal'.
tamevatthamanuppattiyā.translation_2: for the attainment of that very goal, I made strong effort.

nāḷino.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Name of one of the three palaces in the Buddhavaṃsa. Nominative singular in the text (also metrically nāḷino). Possibly related to nāḷi/nāḷikā (lotus stalk), but treated as a proper name here.
nāḷino.translation_2: Kumuda, Nāḷina, and Paduma were his three supreme palaces.

upasirī.meaning_2: name of a palace (Upasirī); glory; splendour
upasirī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Name of one of the three palaces of Buddha Vipassī (with Sirī and Vaḍḍha). Nominative singular in the text; the PEU treats it as a proper name of a mansion.

dhanañcuyyānamuttame.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of dhanañjuyyāne (locative of dhanañjuyyāna, the Dhanañjaya park) + uttame (locative of uttama, supreme); j + u elided. Locative in the text. Both parts decline together.
dhanañcuyyānamuttame.translation_2: That great hero set in motion the Wheel [of Dhamma] in the supreme Dhanañjaya Park.

upasālo.meaning_2: name of a chief disciple of the Buddha; Upasāla
upasālo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name of one of the two chief disciples of the Buddha Gotama in the Buddhavaṃsa verse; nominative singular in the text.
upasālo.example_2: 21. Sālo ca upasālo ca, ahesuṃ aggasāvakā;
upasālo.translation_2: Sāla and Upasāla were the chief disciples.

bodhayitvā.meaning_2: having awakened; having enlightened; having made known
bodhayitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive of the causative bodheti (to awaken, enlighten). In the verse it describes the Buddha awakening matured beings completely.
bodhayitvā.translation_2: Having entirely awakened beings whose minds are mature,

tamajjhapatvā.meaning_2: having fallen upon; having pounced on; having alighted on
tamajjhapatvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text tamajjhapatvā is tam + ajjhapatvā after sandhi; the object is the tree. The reading and analysis are uncertain (ajjhopatvā / ajjhapattā are possible); the meaning is taken from the context 'having arrived at that tree'.
tamajjhapatvā.translation_2: Having arrived at that (tree), he sat down beneath the Mahāsoṇa tree.

asesamabhivāhayi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text asesamabhivāhayi is a past tense form (aorist-like) with the sense of ‘he removed completely’. Possibly an irregular aorist of abhivāhati; the prefix abhi and the absolutive-like form are uncertain. The word occurs in a verse describing the destruction of all defilements.
asesamabhivāhayi.translation_2: There he entirely removed all defilements;

saparijjanaṃ.meaning_2: with attendants; together with the retinue
saparijjanaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it agrees with sasaṅghaṃ in the accusative singular describing the Buddha. Alternative spelling saparijana.
saparijjanaṃ.translation_2: Then I also (honored) the peerless and unparalleled (Buddha), with his assembly and retinue,

hāsetva.meaning_2: having made laugh; having gladdened; having delighted
hāsetva.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive of the causative hāseti (from √has). The form hāsetvā occurs in the verse, metrically shortened here to hāsetva. The causative sense 'make laugh; gladden, delight' fits the context 'hāsetva mānasaṃ' (having gladdened the mind).
hāsetva.example_2: 17. Tassāpi vacanaṃ sutvā, bhiyyo hāsetva mānasaṃ;
hāsetva.translation_2: 17. After hearing that word, I greatly gladdened my heart;

phaggunī.meaning_2: name of the constellation Phaggunī; name of a female disciple (Phagguṇī Therī)
phaggunī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it appears in the nominative singular together with Uttarā; one of the two chief female disciples of a past Buddha. The PEU derives it from phaggu + gaha, but a proper-name analysis is clearer here.
phaggunī.translation_2: 24. Uttarā and Phagguṇī were the chief female disciples.

undī.meaning_2: name of a female lay follower; Undī
undī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name of one of the chief female lay followers (aggupaṭṭhikā) of the Buddha, listed with Indāvarī. The commentary gives the variant gaṇḍī. Doubtful derivation; probably not related to undana or undura. Nominative singular in the text.
undī.example_1: Indāvarī ca vaṇḍī [undī (sī.), gaṇḍī (syā. kaṃ.)] ca, ahesuṃ aggupaṭṭhikā.
undī.translation_1: Indāvarī and Undī were the chief female lay followers.

salaloti.meaning_2: pine tree; name of the bodhi tree of the Buddha
salaloti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The form in the text is salalo ti (salalo + iti), quoted as a name. In the given sentence it is the subject of pavuccati.
salaloti.translation_2: the bodhi (tree) of that Blessed One is called Salala.

damayī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text the form is damayī, an optional 3rd singular present ending (-ī for -eti), used of the Buddha taming the yakkha Kumbhakaṇṇa. The PEU entry analyses it as damu + ṇaya + ī.
damayī.example_2: 5. Punāparaṃ kumbhakaṇṇaṃ, yakkhaṃ so damayī jino;
damayī.translation_2: 5. Again, on another occasion, that Victor tamed the yakṣa named Kumbhakaṇṇa;

pabbajjañcābhirocayiṃ.meaning_2: and I delighted in the going forth; and I approved of renunciation
pabbajjañcābhirocayiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of pabbajjaṃ (accusative of pabbajjā) with ca and abhirocayiṃ (aorist, 1st person singular of abhiroceti, 'delighted in'). Could also be analysed as pabbajjañ ca abhirocayiṃ.
pabbajjañcābhirocayiṃ.translation_2: I went for refuge to him, and delighted in renunciation.

tisoḷasasahassāni.meaning_2: forty-eight thousand; three times sixteen thousand
tisoḷasasahassāni.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound number. In the text it agrees with nāriyo (nom. pl. nt form used with feminine noun).
tisoḷasasahassāni.translation_2: 20. Forty-eight thousand adorned ladies attended him;

upāgañchi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 3rd singular of upagacchati, with ā- prefix; sandhi of upa + ā. Used with sakko as subject.
upāgañchi.translation_2: 4. When Sakka approached the Guide with his retinue;

vicikoḷi.meaning_2: name of a woman (chief consort of the Bodhisatta Puññavaḍḍhana)
vicikoḷi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name in the Buddhavaṃsa verse. Nominative singular in the text. The PEU suggests vicita + olī but this is uncertain; kept uncompounded here. Some editions may read vicikoli.
vicikoḷi.translation_2: The woman (chief consort) was named Vicikoḷi, and his son was Puññavaḍḍhana.

sālisā.meaning_2: name of a female lay disciple (together with Kaḷī)
sālisā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text reads sālisā, the reading of the Burmese edition; the Siamese and Cambodian editions read sāḷiyā. The form is most likely a nominative plural of a name in -ī, sālisī, alongside kaḷiyā (kaḷī). If instead it is an ablative or instrumental of sāḷi (rice), the meaning would be 'from rice'.
sālisā.example_1: Sāḷiyā [sālisā (syā. kaṃ.)] ca kaḷiyā ca, ahesuṃ aggupaṭṭhikā.
sālisā.translation_1: Sāḷiyā and Kaḷiyā were his chief female lay followers.

kaḷiyā.meaning_2: Kaḷiyā; name of a female lay disciple
kaḷiyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name; paired with Sāḷiyā, chief female lay followers of Buddha Dhammadassī. Nominative singular in the text.
kaḷiyā.example_2: Sāḷiyā [sālisā (syā. kaṃ.)] ca kaḷiyā ca, ahesuṃ aggupaṭṭhikā.
kaḷiyā.translation_2: Sāḷiyā and Kaḷiyā were his chief female lay followers.

pupphāpetvāna.meaning_2: having caused to blossom; having made flourish
pupphāpetvāna.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive in -tvāna of the causative pupphāpeti. In the verse it is used figuratively of the Buddha making his disciples flourish. Text variants may read pupphāpetvā.
pupphāpetvāna.translation_2: 23. Having shown abundant radiance and caused his disciples to spiritually flourish;

vilāsetvā.meaning_2: having sported; having enjoyed oneself; having played
vilāsetvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive in -tvā of the causative vilāseti (vi + √laḷ). In the verse it describes sporting in jhānas and attainments before final nibbāna.
vilāsetvā.translation_2: having sported in (mundane and supramundane) attainments, he attained final extinguishment together with his disciples.

āmaṇḍoti.meaning_2: name of a tree (the Bodhi tree of the Buddha); castor oil plant; walnut tree
āmaṇḍoti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The form āmaṇḍoti is āmaṇḍa + iti (quotation). In the Buddhavaṃsa it names the Bodhi tree of a Buddha. The commentary identifies it with the walnut tree (Juglans regia).
āmaṇḍoti.translation_2: the Bodhi tree of that Blessed One is called the āmaṇḍa tree.

parimocayi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 3rd singular of the causative parimoceti, used transitively with the ablative bandhanā ('from bonds').
parimocayi.translation_2: 34. He released many devas and humans from bonds.

tīṇiyojanaso.meaning_2: for three leagues; three yojanas in extent
tīṇiyojanaso.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of tīṇi and yojanaso; yojanaso is an adverbial accusative/ablative-type form meaning 'by three yojanas'. None of the listed parts fit exactly under one pos, so treated as sandhi of a numeral and an adverbial noun form (masc).
tīṇiyojanaso.translation_2: Radiance emanated for three leagues in all directions.

pavassetvā.meaning_2: having caused to rain; having poured down
pavassetvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative absolutive of pavassati; in the verse it takes dhammameghaṃ as object, 'having caused the rain of Dhamma to fall'. Sometimes written pavassitvā.
pavassetvā.translation_2: 26. Having caused the rain of Dhamma to fall, and having soaked beings with their devas,

pāpayitvāna.meaning_2: having caused to reach; having led (to)
pāpayitvāna.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive in -tvāna of the causative pāpeti (from √ap with pa + apa). In the text: khemantaṃ pāpayitvāna, 'having led (them) to the safe place', i.e. Nibbāna.
pāpayitvāna.translation_2: and having led them to Nibbāna, the safe place, he became fully quenched together with his disciples.

paṇitaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular masculine agreeing with dhammaṃ. Sometimes spelt paṇīta; the text's paṇitaṃ is a variant spelling.
paṇitaṃ.translation_2: Having heard that excellent Dhamma, I delighted in the going forth.

pabbajjamabhirocayiṃ.meaning_2: came to like; was pleased (with); took delight (in)
pabbajjamabhirocayiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi resolution of pabbajjaṃ abhirocayiṃ (pabbajjaṃ + abhirocayiṃ), first person singular aorist. Related to pabbajjā.
pabbajjamabhirocayiṃ.translation_2: Having heard that excellent Dhamma, I delighted in the going forth.

rocinī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name of a brahmin woman, consort of the Buddha Kakusandha. Nominative singular in the text.
rocinī.example_2: Rocinī nāma sā nārī, uttaro nāma atrajo.
rocinī.translation_2: that woman was named Rocinī, and his son was named Uttara.

pavāhiya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive in -tvā with the -tvā > -ya sandhi. Used with malaṃ in the sense of washing away stains.
pavāhiya.translation_2: and having washed away all stains, he attained supreme awakening.

maccuyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Instrumental singular maccuyā. In the compound bhijjitānañca maccuyā, 'shattered by death' or 'broken by death' (i.e., destroyed by death).
maccuyā.translation_2: who had transcended the floods and shattered death.

samussetvā.meaning_2: having set up; having established; having raised
samussetvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive in -tvā of the causative samusseti; used with dhammacetiṃ (accusative) in the text.
samussetvā.translation_2: 27. Having established the Dhamma monument, adorned with the banner of Dhamma,

sañchaḍḍitaṃ.meaning_2: thrown away; abandoned; given up completely
sañchaḍḍitaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Agrees with kulamūlaṃ (neuter nominative or accusative singular). The PEU suggests saṃ + chadita, but the text and meaning point to saṃ + chaḍḍita from √chaḍḍ.
sañchaḍḍitaṃ.translation_2: 2. Having completely given up the family home and its many foods, drinks, and provisions;

bodhayī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 3rd singular bodhayī in the text (causative aorist of bujjhati). PTS lists bodhayi as aorist. Alternative lemma bodheti.
bodhayī.translation_2: the Victor caused three crores of thousands of devas to awaken.

saṃthomayantā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Masculine nominative plural agreeing with janā. Causal form of saṃthomayati; the PEU analysis treats thoma as the base with a ṇaya suffix.
saṃthomayantā.translation_1: 12. Always delighting in the Dhamma, praising the noble path, these people,
